answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie voting weight to costly work that cannot be transferred between identities. A verifier can issue a short cipher style challenge bound to a fresh seed, so an operator who spins up a thousand copies of an agent gains nothing, because each copy must solve its own puzzle. Reputation should build slowly, like a marble rolling down a ridge, and claims from suspicious clusters that answer with near identical solutions can be discounted. Even a carved ivory seal would not fool the network if the work behind it is unique to each participant.
